kus: KU1. • Fundamental Principles of Biomedical Instrumentation:

pcs.pc_description: Student demonstrates an understanding of the fundamental principles underlying the design and development of biomedical instrumentation, including signal processing, sensor technologies, and system integration.

Student applies theoretical knowledge to practical scenarios by designing and prototyping biomedical instruments, incorporating appropriate sensors, amplifiers, and signal conditioning circuits to achieve accurate and reliable measurements.

Student evaluates the performance of biomedical instruments through experimental testing, identifies areas for improvement, and optimizes design parameters to enhance accuracy, sensitivity, and usability.

Student demonstrates proficiency in utilizing a variety of biomedical techniques such as bio-electric potentials, cardiovascular analysis, microscopic examination, and pH measurement, accurately interpreting experimental data and results.

Student designs and executes experiments effectively, selecting appropriate techniques and instrumentation to address specific biomedical research questions or diagnostic challenges, while considering factors such as sample preparation, data acquisition, and analysis.

Student analyzes experimental data using statistical methods, graphical visualization, and qualitative analysis techniques, interpreting results to draw meaningful conclusions and make informed decisions in biomedical diagnostics and research.

modules.module_title: Integration of Computing in Biomedical Domain

pcs.pc_description: Student understands the principles of digital computing and microprocessor-based systems, including programming languages, data structures, algorithms, and interfacing techniques relevant to biomedical applications.

Student integrates computing technologies with biomedical instrumentation effectively, designing software interfaces, developing data acquisition and processing algorithms, and implementing control systems to enhance the functionality and performance of biomedical devices.

Student troubleshoots software and hardware issues in biomedical computing systems, employing systematic debugging techniques, diagnostic tools, and problem-solving strategies to identify and resolve technical problems in a timely manner.
